newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HAMPTON THROWS COMPLETE GAME AS ASTROS BEAT EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HAMPTON THROWS COMPLETE GAME AS ASTROS BEAT EXPOS.

text.p: Mike Hampton tossed his fourth complete game in six July starts as the Houston Astros matched their longest winning streak since 1991 with their ninth straight victory Sunday, 7-2 over the slumping Montreal Expos.
Hampton (8-7) gave up eight hits, struck out six and walked none for the National League Central Division leaders.
The left-hander is 5-0 with a 2.25 earned run average in July, giving up just 12 earned runs in 48 innings. He had just two complete games in his career before this month.

"I feel strong and my arm feels great," Hampton said. "Right now I have the mindset that this is my game and I want to finish it. I'm pitching with a lot of confidence right now. All I'm trying to do is throw strikes, keep the hitters off-balance and let the team score some runs for me."
Sean Berry homered, tripled, drove in three runs and scored twice for the Astros, who swept a four-game series for the first time since August 2-5 against Atlanta.
Jim Bullinger (6-10) yielded seven runs and eight hits in 5 1/3 innings and has lost four of his last five decisions. The Expos lost for the eighth time in nine games.

In Cincinnati, Greg Maddux allowed one run over six innings to win his eighth straight start and become the National League's first 15-game winner and Mark Lemke drove in two runs as the Atlanta Braves beat the Reds 3-2.
Maddux (15-3), gave up four hits with a walk and five strikeouts. He has not lost since June 13 against Baltimore and his last defeat against a National League team came on June 2 against San Diego.
Mark Wohlers surrendered a run in the ninth but struck out Hal Morris looking to end the game for his 25th save in 27 opportunities.
The Braves widened their lead in the East to 6 1/2 games over the Marlins and Mets.

In San Diego, Ken Caminiti delivered a run-scoring double and Wally Joyner had an RBI single, both with two outs, in a three-run seventh as the red-hot Padres beat the New York Mets 5-3 in the rubber game of their three-game set.
Former Mets farmhand Quilvio Veras had four hits and Tony Gwynn added a key sacrifice fly for the Padres, who have won seven of their last eight games.
San Diego, which is 14-4 since the All-Star break, has won four straight series.
The Padres got two sparkling plays from Padres centre fielder Steve Finley and one by third baseman Ken Caminiti.

In St. Louis, Delino DeShields homered twice and drove in three runs and Andy Benes struck out seven in 6 2/3 innings for his first win in more than a month as the Cardinals defeated the Florida Marlins 6-4.
DeShields, who also belted a pinch two-run homer on Saturday, had the second two-homer game of his career. His second homer was the 1,000th hit of his career.
Benes (7-5) allowed both runs, four hits and three walks to lower his ERA to 3.06.
In San Francisco, the Giants and Pirates split a doubleheader.
In the opener, pinch-running pitcher Shawn Estes scored from third on a wild pitch by Marc Wilkins (6-2) with one out in the bottom of the 13th, giving the Giants a 6-5 victory.

San Francisco averted a season-high four-game losing streak, no thanks to Rod Beck, who blew his fourth save in 35 chances, allowing a pair of tying runs in the ninth. Doug Henry (3-4) pitched a scoreless 13th and got the win.
In the second game, Kevin Young hit a pair of two-run homers and Tony Womack went 4-for-5 with an RBI as the Pirates held on for a 10-7 victory.
Jose Guillen also had a two-run homer for the Pirates.
Second-place Pittsburgh fell five behind Houston in the Central with just its second loss in 12 games at 3Com Park. The Giants' lead over the Dodgers shrank to 1 1/2 games in the West.
In Los Angeles, Roger Cedeno homered to trigger a five-run sixth inning and Tom Candiotti (7-3) improved to 4-1 as a starter as the Dodgers beat the Philadelphia Phillies 7-1.
Tripp Cromer also homered and scored twice for Los Angeles, which beat the Phillies for the seventh straight time.
Raul Mondesi stole a base to become just the second player in Dodger history with two 20-20 seasons. Pedro Guerrero accomplished the feat in 1982-83.

At Colorado, rookie John Thomson and Darren Holmes combined on a seven-hit shutout, just the 13th in Rockies history, as they won their fifth straight game and completed a four-game sweep of the Chicago Cubs, 4-0.

Thomson (3-6) allowed six hits and a walk over the first eight innings, striking out a career-high eight. Thomson, who snapped a six-start winless streak, has allowed just two runs and 19 hits in his last 22 innings. Holmes allowed a single in the ninth but held Chicago scoreless.
Neifi Perez homered for Colorado.
